comparison: Perfect agreement on C25-C33. Both evaluate the electrophysiological and molecular characterization of MPO Nts neurons as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes converging evidence and internal consistency; peer reviewers describe the work as 'carefully executed' with 'convincing evidence' and note the expertise in intracellular recordings.

Perfect agreement on C34-C40. Both evaluate the dual inhibitory-excitatory mechanism as SUPPORTED. OpenEval praises the systematic pharmacological dissection; peer reviewers unanimously praise this as a key contribution, with Reviewer 1 highlighting the opposing physiologic effects of GABA and Nts from the same neurons.

Disagreement on C41-C49. OpenEval evaluates temporal dissociation evidence as SUPPORTED with strong pharmacological controls. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 3 noting 'co-release of GABA and Nts is primarily inferred rather than directly proven' and requesting more direct evidence.

Perfect agreement on C53-C56. Both evaluate the GABA deletion experiments as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes the striking reversal from hyperthermia to hypothermia; peer reviewers describe this as 'elegant' and central to demonstrating opposing roles of GABA and Nts.

Agreement on C57-C63. Both evaluate unmasking of excitatory effects in VGAT knockout as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes converging evidence from multiple approaches; peer reviewers accept the genetic manipulation and resulting physiological changes without concerns. Peer R5 also includes C64 (validation), which OpenEval addresses separately in R7.

OpenEval R7 addresses C64 (knockout validation) as SUPPORTED, emphasizing its critical importance. Peer R5 includes C64 along with C57-C63 and evaluates all as SUPPORTED, accepting the validation without specific comment.

Partial overlap on C65-C66. OpenEval evaluates fever dynamics as SUPPORTED while acknowledging interpretive uncertainty. Peer R6 covers C65-C73 and rates as UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 3 noting context-dependent effects require more detailed explanation. OpenEval addresses C67-C73 separately in R9-R11.

Partial overlap on C67-C69. OpenEval evaluates heat loss control as SUPPORTED with appropriate statistics. Peer R6 includes these claims in a broader UNCERTAIN evaluation (C65-C73), noting complexity of context-dependent effects at different ambient temperatures.

Partial overlap on C70. OpenEval evaluates circadian pattern changes as SUPPORTED while noting speculation about mechanisms. Peer R6 includes C70 in broader UNCERTAIN evaluation of C65-C73, requesting more detailed explanation for context-dependent effects.

Partial overlap on C71-C73. Both evaluate cold exposure results as UNCERTAIN. OpenEval notes contradiction with predictions and speculative explanations. Peer R6 includes these in broader evaluation requesting more detailed explanation for ambient temperature-dependent effects.

Partial overlap on C114-C116. Both evaluate as UNCERTAIN. OpenEval notes unexpected phenotype contradicting local GABA effects with speculative explanations. Peer R11 requests more detailed explanation for context-dependent effects and notes contradictions with previous literature.

Perfect agreement on C74-C78. Both evaluate pharmacological dissection as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes strong evidence for MPO localization with 76% blockade. Peer reviewers accept this without question, though Reviewer 3 notes differences between optogenetic and chemogenetic methods warrant investigation.

Disagreement on C79-C86. OpenEval evaluates chemogenetic characterization as SUPPORTED with comprehensive data. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 3 noting differences between optogenetic and chemogenetic methods not thoroughly investigated and requesting comparison of release patterns.

Disagreement on C87-C92. OpenEval evaluates synthesis of dual transmitter model as SUPPORTED with well-supported temporal dynamics. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 3 stating co-release is 'primarily inferred rather than directly proven.'

Agreement on C93-C97. Both evaluate theoretical interpretations as UNCERTAIN. OpenEval notes these are reasonable hypotheses requiring experimental validation. Peer reviewers do not specifically comment on these speculative functional mechanisms.

Disagreement on C118-C121. OpenEval evaluates torpor connection as SUPPORTED based on literature and magnitude of hypothermia, noting speculation about initiation. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 2 stating this connection deserves 'greater consideration (albeit speculative)' and is underdeveloped.

Perfect agreement on C122-C126. Both evaluate speculative mechanisms for chemogenetic differences as UNCERTAIN. OpenEval notes lack of direct experimental support; peer reviewers note differences between methods not thoroughly investigated.

Perfect agreement on background literature (C1-C24). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes accurate representation of prior work; peer reviewers accept this well-established context without question. Peer R14 also includes C51 not in OpenEval R18.

Partial overlap on C99-C105. OpenEval evaluates prior literature as SUPPORTED for context. Peer R10 also includes C98, C106 and evaluates connection to Adcyap1 neurons as SUPPORTED, while noting torpor connection is underdeveloped.

Partial overlap on C109-C112, C114-C115. OpenEval evaluates prior literature on context-dependent GABA effects as SUPPORTED. Peer R11 includes these in broader UNCERTAIN evaluation of contradictory findings, requesting more detailed explanation.

Minimal overlap on C50. OpenEval R4 evaluates local circuit organization (C50, C52, C98) as SUPPORTED, noting negative findings are appropriately reported. Peer R3 focuses on C41-C50 regarding co-release evidence and rates as UNCERTAIN.

Minimal overlap on C98. OpenEval R4 evaluates identification of Adcyap1 targets as SUPPORTED. Peer R10 includes C98 in broader evaluation of Adcyap1 connection as SUPPORTED, noting torpor link is underdeveloped.
Minimal overlap on C106. OpenEval R16 evaluates synthesis showing MPO vs brain-wide effects as SUPPORTED. Peer R10 includes C106 in evaluation of Adcyap1 connection as SUPPORTED.

OpenEval R20 evaluates abstract-level summary claims (C4-C12) as SUPPORTED, noting they are well-supported by detailed experimental results. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these summary claims.
